method: Headlines collected via web search (fetch_news.py collector blocked in sandbox; use it for local/Actions runs). Entity sentiment scored by Claude during the weekly Cowork routine. sentiment = 0-100 D-favorability of coverage tone (matches existing dashboard sentimentScore semantics: >55 leans D, <45 leans R). candidateSentiment = 0-100 favorability of coverage toward that candidate personally. outletLean: -2 left ... +2 right (AllSides-style); null = unrated outlet, excluded from scatter.

races.matchup: Susan Collins (R, inc.) vs. Troy Jackson (D)
races.summary: Jackson (D) holds a narrow lead over incumbent Collins (R) in an increasingly competitive, high-spending race, with Fox News showing Jackson +2 (Aug. 6-10) and an Abacus poll +9 in late August, though Collins overcame similar 2020 deficits. Late-August coverage centers on a debate dispute (Collins accepted four local TV debates but declined a CNN/BDN one) and a wave of misleading attack ads from both sides. Cook Political Report rates the race a toss-up.

races.matchup: Hannah Pingree (D) vs. Bobby Charles (R) vs. Rick Bennett (I)
races.summary: Coverage of the open-seat race to succeed term-limited Gov. Janet Mills was limited and older in this window, dominated by polling that showed Democrat Hannah Pingree with a comfortable double-digit lead over Republican Bobby Charles, with independent Rick Bennett in single digits. Additional reporting covered debate negotiations, with Pingree and Bennett agreeing to four televised debates while Charles pushed for a larger town-hall series. Tone leaned Democratic, driven mainly by Pingree's polling advantage.

races.summary: Coverage in late August focused on a string of polls showing Democrat Abdul El-Sayed with narrow leads over Republican Mike Rogers in the open race for retiring Sen. Gary Peters's seat, with margins ranging from a dead heat to seven points. Reporting also covered heavy Republican outside spending to boost Rogers and the candidates' contrasting positions on data centers. Tone leaned modestly Democratic on favorable polling, though outlets stressed the race remains a genuine toss-up.

races.summary: Benson (D) holds narrow, within-margin leads over James (R) in the open-seat governor's race, 45-41 in a late-August EPIC-MRA poll (fielded Aug. 22-28) and 47-38 in an early-August EPIC-MRA survey. Both candidates won their Aug. 4 primaries; James carries Trump's endorsement. Coverage frames the contest as competitive but tilting slightly Democratic amid weak Trump approval and economic pessimism among Michigan voters.

Michigan governor's race enters general election after Benson, James primary wins

races.matchup: Jon Husted (R, inc.) vs. Sherrod Brown (D)
races.summary: Coverage was dominated by data centers as a defining issue, with reporting on Democrat Sherrod Brown's ad campaign hammering appointed GOP Sen. Jon Husted over tax breaks he backed as lieutenant governor, and on Husted recalibrating his stance and pushing ratepayer-protection legislation. National coverage highlighted a leaked NRSC memo warning that data-center backlash is endangering the GOP's hold on the seat, alongside polling and fundraising advantages for Brown. Tone leaned Democratic, framing the issue landscape and momentum in Brown's favor.

articles.headline: Republicans concerned over the role data centers play in Ohio's elections

Ohio's US Senate candidates recalibrate their stances on data centers

races.summary: The Ohio governor's race remains a dead heat entering September, with dueling August polls showing Ramaswamy up 50-48 (Fox News) and Acton up 47-46 (Wedgewood). Coverage centers on the record-breaking spending gap (Ramaswamy has spent roughly $21M to Acton's $5.5M) and sharp messaging: Ramaswamy's ads cast him as a business innovator while Democratic groups, including the DGA, brand him a self-funding 'conman' out of touch with Ohioans. Recent reporting focused on how the two are defining themselves and each other on issues like immigration enforcement and property taxes.

races.summary: Cooper (D) leads Whatley (R) across August polling, ranging from +5 in a High Point University poll (released Aug. 21) to +11 in the Elon University poll (Aug. 12). Coverage tone favors Cooper but increasingly flags a tightening race as Whatley, Trump's endorsed candidate and former RNC chair, gains name recognition. Cook Political Report rates the open Tillis seat Lean Democrat.

races.matchup: Jon Ossoff (D, inc.) vs. Mike Collins (R)
races.summary: Democratic incumbent Jon Ossoff holds a steady lead over Trump-backed Rep. Mike Collins, with August polls ranging from +7 (InsiderAdvantage, Aug 16-17) to +13 (Fox News). Coverage highlights Ossoff's rallies attacking Trump and Collins on affordability and the Iran war, his cash-on-hand advantage, and a trio of Republican endorsements he has secured. Collins drew negative attention over a former campaign staffer who posed in a KKK uniform and posted a swastika online, and over a Savannah exchange about compensating Jan. 6 defendants.

races.matchup: Rick Jackson (R) vs. Keisha Lance Bottoms (D)
races.summary: The open-seat race to succeed term-limited Gov. Brian Kemp is effectively tied, with an InsiderAdvantage poll showing Jackson at 46.3% and Bottoms at 46.2%. Coverage was dominated by an intensifying character fight: Bottoms confronted Jackson in person over an ad referencing her family ('stay away from my family'), while Jackson and Kemp sharpened attacks on her record as Atlanta mayor over spending and crime. Both candidates centered 'character' in weekend campaign events, and Jackson launched a large ad blitz focused on affordability and Bottoms's mayoral tenure.

races.summary: The race for retiring Sen. Joni Ernst's seat has become surprisingly competitive: a late-August Suffolk University poll showed Hinson leading Turek 45-41, within the margin of error, and Cook Political Report shifted the race from 'leans Republican' to 'toss-up.' Coverage featured Hinson attacking Turek's Iowa House attendance and immigration record, Sen. Ted Cruz headlining a Hinson fundraiser where he called Democrats 'Marxists and Islamists,' and Democrats hitting Hinson over her handling of the Epstein-files votes. Turek, a Paralympian, has leaned on cancer-advocacy and bipartisan messaging.

races.summary: Coverage in the back half of August framed Rob Sand as the front-runner after an Emerson College/Nexstar poll put him up 48-43 and Cook Political Report shifted the race from toss-up to Lean Democratic. Much of the reporting centered on the campaign turning negative, with GOP nominee Zach Lahn accusing Sand of personal attacks over his residency and family and Sand publicly calling for civility. National profiles emphasized Sand's attempt to run as a nonpartisan independent-minded Democrat, while Lahn leaned into an anti-establishment message after upsetting Trump-endorsed Rep. Randy Feenstra in the primary.

races.matchup: Joe Lombardo (R, inc.) vs. Aaron Ford (D)
races.summary: August coverage leaned toward an incumbent-momentum narrative: three GOP-affiliated polls showed Gov. Joe Lombardo opening a 7-12 point lead, and reporting stressed his roughly $13 million advertising advantage over AG Aaron Ford, who only went on air late in the month. A running story line was a bitter fight over misrepresented law-enforcement and Democratic endorsements between the two campaigns. Ford's messaging tied Lombardo to a 'Lombardo-Trump economy' and affordability concerns, but nonpartisan aggregates still rated the contest a near dead-heat toss-up.

articles.headline: Three New Polls Show Lombardo Expanding Lead Over Ford in Nevada Governor's Race

races.summary: With the general election set after Crowley's razor-thin Aug. 11 primary win over Francesca Hong, coverage gave Democrat David Crowley a modest early edge: a Marquette Law School poll had him up 49-44 among likely voters (tied among registered) and a separate Badger Battleground poll showed a four-point lead with stronger favorability than Republican Rep. Tom Tiffany, whose numbers ran underwater. Reporting repeatedly tied Tiffany to Trump's sagging approval while noting Crowley's need to unify progressives and build name recognition. Both sides launched seven-figure attack-ad campaigns, and analysts stressed Wisconsin's tradition of razor-close statewide races.

races.matchup: Katie Hobbs (D, inc.) vs. Andy Biggs (R)
races.summary: August coverage was dominated by polls showing Democratic Gov. Katie Hobbs with a comfortable lead over Republican Rep. Andy Biggs, ranging from an 8-point AARP-commissioned margin to 13- and 15-point leads in HighGround and Noble Predictive Insights surveys, powered by a wide advantage among independents. Reporting noted Biggs still needed to consolidate GOP voters after his July primary. Coverage also framed the contest as immediately negative and attack-filled, with both candidates targeting the other's long-standing vulnerabilities.

races.matchup: Chris Pappas (D) vs. John E. Sununu (R)
races.summary: Coverage of the open Shaheen seat trended slightly toward a Republican-momentum story in late August, as a UNH Survey Center poll (Aug. 20-24) showed former Sen. John E. Sununu narrowly edging Democratic Rep. Chris Pappas 45-43, a reversal from Pappas's earlier lead. Conservative outlets highlighted the seat as an under-the-radar GOP flip opportunity backed by heavy national super PAC spending, while other reporting stressed the race's relative lack of extremes and its persistent toss-up status. Both remain their parties' clear front-runners ahead of the Sept. 8 primary.

races.matchup: Kelly Ayotte (R, inc.) vs. Cinde Warmington (D)
races.summary: Coverage over the last two weeks was dominated by a UNH Survey Center poll released Aug. 27 showing Gov. Kelly Ayotte leading presumptive Democratic nominee Cinde Warmington 49%-39%, with her job approval improving. Reporting framed Ayotte as strengthening her position while Warmington, who still faces a Sept. 8 primary as the presumptive nominee, campaigns on affordability. Tone was largely factual and poll-driven, tilting favorable to the Republican incumbent.

races.summary: With term-limited Gov. Laura Kelly departing, coverage framed this as one of Republicans' best gubernatorial pickup opportunities but noted the general is shaping up close. Trump-endorsed state Senate President Ty Masterson and Democratic state Sen. Cindy Holscher emerged from their Aug. 4 primaries. A late-August poll (published Aug. 28) showed Holscher edging Masterson 47-46, within the margin of error, with Holscher strong among unaffiliated and moderate voters. Tone is roughly neutral with a slight D tilt reflecting the early polling lead.

races.matchup: Kurt Alme (R) vs. Alani Bankhead (D) vs. Seth Bodnar (I)
races.summary: Coverage centered on Democratic disarray ahead of the Aug. 10 ballot-withdrawal deadline: Democratic nominee Alani Bankhead defied intense pressure to exit, declaring she will stay through Nov. 3, while party figures including Jon Tester and Max Baucus rallied behind independent Seth Bodnar, the former University of Montana president who leads all candidates in fundraising. Reporting stressed that a Bankhead-Bodnar split of the anti-MAGA vote likely clears a path for Republican Kurt Alme, with polls showing Alme winning comfortably in three- or four-way scenarios. Tone is unfavorable toward Democrats given the emphasis on intra-party dysfunction.

races.matchup: Dan Sullivan (R, inc.) vs. Mary Peltola (D)
races.summary: After the Aug. 18 all-party primary, Sen. Dan Sullivan and Democrat Mary Peltola advanced to a November ranked-choice showdown that most coverage frames as a genuine battleground and a Democratic pickup opportunity. Recent polls and betting markets give Peltola a narrow but consistent edge, and reporting leans toward her as the early front-runner. Coverage is dominated by the chaos of a second candidate named Dan Sullivan on the ballot, which GOP allies call a plot to confuse voters and which is now under federal investigation. Sullivan has gone on the attack in the first post-primary faceoff as he tries to close a small polling gap.

races.matchup: Pete Ricketts (R, inc.) vs. Dan Osborn (I)
races.summary: Republican Sen. Pete Ricketts leads independent Dan Osborn by roughly five to six points in polling averages, though Osborn, who took 47% against Sen. Deb Fischer in 2024, is again treated as a serious challenger in a race described as heated. Much of the recent coverage centers on ballot and legal drama, including a court fight over whether Nebraska Democrats must field a replacement Senate candidate. The two are set to meet Sept. 1 in the only scheduled debate, at the Nebraska State Fair. Conservative commentary has attacked Osborn's independent label as a Democratic front, keeping the partisan framing sharp.

articles.headline: Nebraska State Fair will host US Senate debate between Osborn, Ricketts

races.summary: Coverage of the Texas Senate race turned decisively toward Democrat James Talarico in late August after the Cook Political Report moved the contest from lean Republican to toss-up on Aug. 20, citing Attorney General Ken Paxton's scandals and underwater favorability. Multiple polls show Talarico narrowly leading or tied, and reporting emphasizes his fundraising advantage and strong support among Black and Latino voters. Even right-leaning outlets describe Paxton as deeply flawed and underperforming a generic Republican, while his campaign insists Texas will stay red. Paxton beat incumbent John Cornyn in the May 26 GOP runoff, and the general election is now among the most closely watched in the country.

races.matchup: Greg Abbott (R, inc.) vs. Gina Hinojosa (D)
races.summary: Gov. Greg Abbott continues to lead Democrat Gina Hinojosa, but by a narrowing margin of roughly four to seven points, and the Cook Political Report shifted the race from solid Republican to likely Republican, calling Hinojosa surprisingly competitive. Coverage highlights Hinojosa's rising favorability and momentum as more voters learn who she is, alongside Abbott's slipping job approval. Reporting also notes Abbott's enormous fundraising and cash-on-hand advantage over Hinojosa's comparatively small war chest. Some pieces spotlight Texas conservatives breaking ranks, though most analysts still rate Abbott the clear favorite for a fourth term.
